ConceptRequest.description:
A root term plus any concept parameters to override. Omitted parameters take their
defaults; `steps` defaults to the λ the model's X′ was walked with for `refs`.

The reference terms (and so Q) are the model's, fixed when it was built, so there's no `q`.
`trim_ratio`, `threshold`, `root_weight`, and `stored_terms` only reshape the scoring of the
root's walk: changing them reuses an earlier concept's walk of the same root.

info.description:
Concepts and ranked semantic search over co-occurrence models
([Markovian Semantic Relatedness](https://github.com/KPreisner/markovian-semantic-relatedness)).

**How a request flows**
1. Pick a model (`GET /models`) and a root term (`GET /models/{model_id}/terms?prefix=`).
2. `POST /models/{model_id}/concepts`: `200 ready` with a `concept_id` if it's cached, otherwise
   `202 pending` with the `job_id` building it. Identical requests share one job.
3. Follow the job: `GET /jobs/{job_id}/events` streams its progress as Server-Sent Events and
   ends with `result` (or `error`); `GET /jobs/{job_id}` is the same state for polling.
4. `GET /concepts/{concept_id}` is the ranked table. `POST /searches` with one or more concepts
   and a corpus (`GET /corpora`) starts a search job the same way; `GET /searches/{search_id}`
   has its hits.

Terms are case-sensitive. Every error has one shape: `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"?}}`.
Send `X-Correlation-ID` (a UUID) to trace a request through the logs; the response echoes it.
info.title: Markovian Semantic Relatedness API

get.description:
The stack's health: the API itself, Postgres, Redis, RabbitMQ (with each queue's depth and
consumers), the workers that answer a ping, and the active jobs. 503 when Postgres, Redis, or
RabbitMQ is down; `degraded` (still 200) when no worker answers. Takes about a second: the
worker ping waits for replies. A report is reused for up to `MSR_HEALTH_CACHE_SECONDS`.

The API process is up and serving. Instant and checks nothing else: the container
healthcheck.
The job's durable status, for clients that poll.

get.description:
The job's progress as Server-Sent Events: `progress` events, then one `result` or `error`,
then the stream closes. Reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID` resumes after that event.
Disconnecting never cancels the job.

200.description: An event stream. Each event's `data:` is one JSON object with a `type`: `progress` (`phase`, `step`, `total`, `message`; searches add `bytes_scanned` and `hits`), `result` (`result_id`: the concept or search id), or `error` (`code`, `message`). `id:` is the stream entry id; comment lines are pings.
